canonical_question: Why is cold rolling performed at 25 °C instead of an intermediate temperature to control recrystallization during the strain reduction?

question_variants.question: Why is cold rolling performed at 25 °C instead of an intermediate temperature to control recrystallization during the strain reduction?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document reports the cold rolling temperature as 25 °C (ambient) but does not provide the rationale for this choice, nor does it discuss alternative intermediate temperatures or their potential effects on recrystallization control.

answers.answer: The text specifies the temperature used but offers no explanation for the choice over intermediate temperatures. It states: 'After hot rolling, the ingots were rolled at ambient temperature (25 °C) with a reduction ratio of 75%'.
answers.boundary_limitation: No rationale provided for temperature selection; no comparison to intermediate temperatures.
evidence_spans: Bulk (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (W30-Ni45-Fe20-Ta5, in at.%) alloy ingots were prepared by arc melting pure metals (all with purity >99.99%) in an argon atmosphere.
Alloy samples were repeatedly melted at least 10 times to ensure uniform melting and improve their chemical homogeneity.

After cooling, the bulk ingots with dimensions of 50 mm × 50 mm × 10 mm were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h in an Ar atmosphere and subsequently hot-rolled at 1200 °C with a rolling reduction ratio of 80%, i.e., with a thickness reduction from 10 to 2 mm.

source_evidence_spans: After hot rolling, the ingots were rolled at ambient temperature (25 °C) with a reduction ratio of 75%
